solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Strung out, making noises

indicators.note: letters that are out of place have been knocked from their proper order, so the word is rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone strung out, perhaps on drugs, mumbling and making odd sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Grunts are low guttural sounds, so they are a kind of noise; plural noun matches plural noun.

clue.text: Unloaded weapon held by gangs of men and women

indicators.note: unloaded means emptied of contents, so only the outside letters of the next word remain
held by means kept within, so this piece goes inside the next

blocks.note: the first and last letters of this word
gangs are groups of people

explanation.surface: An empty gun in the hands of armed gangs of both sexes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unloaded weapon' suggests GUN with its middle gone, but it is the word weapon itself that is emptied.
explanation.definitionFit: Grown-ups are adults, so men and women collectively, as opposed to children.

clue.text: Matching costumes for us?

blocks.note: surface reading: identical outfits worn by our team or group
setter's reading: us is the plural of the letter U, and in the NATO alphabet each U is spoken as a word for matching outfits

explanation.walkthrough: 'Us' looks like a pronoun, but it is two letter Us; the radio alphabet's word for U is also matching dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Uniforms are identical outfits worn by members of a group, so matching costumes.

clue.text: Write novel to cover rent that sets mine off

indicators.note: novel means new and different, so the preceding word is made into a fresh arrangement
to cover something is to wrap around it, so the rearranged word goes around the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a rent is a tear, or rip

explanation.surface: An author writes a novel to pay the rent on a property that blows up in their face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' and 'rent' tempt a writer's-life reading; 'mine' is an explosive, not the possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A tripwire is a hidden wire that detonates a mine or trap when someone walks into it.

clue.text: Smiled facetiously and praised me, leaving a mess

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so the letter named after it goes out of the phrase
a mess is a jumble, so the remaining letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the single letter to be removed

explanation.surface: Someone smirked, flattered the speaker, then walked off leaving chaos behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the A from PRAISEDME to leave PRISEDME, then rearrange those eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To simper is to smile in an affected, coy or silly way, which is a facetious smile in past tense.

clue.text: At a picnic, eat badly and weaken

indicators.note: badly means poorly done or wrongly, so these letters come out in the wrong order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Eating dodgy food on an outdoor picnic leaves a person feeling poorly and feeble.
explanation.definitionFit: To incapacitate is to deprive of strength or ability, so to weaken or disable someone.

clue.text: Bent party leader gets mention

indicators.note: the leader is the one at the front, so only the opening letter of the preceding word counts

blocks.note: the first letter of this word
to make a reference is to mention something

explanation.surface: A corrupt party boss is named in the press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent' wants to mean crooked, describing the party leader; it is the noun for an inclination, standing alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A bent is a natural inclination or liking, which is what a preference is.

clue.text: Trade can make it real

indicators.note: can make suggests building something from raw material, so the following letters are refashioned

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Commerce is what turns an idea into something tangible.
explanation.definitionFit: Retail is the business of selling goods to the public, a branch of trade.

clue.text: Lures firm into manufacturing dyes

indicators.note: into means going inside, so this piece is put within the other
manufacturing means processing raw material into new form, so the following letters are reshaped

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A chemical company is tempted into the business of producing colourings.
explanation.definitionFit: Decoys are things used to lure or entice into a trap, so a plural noun for lures.

clue.text: Source uncovered more high wind

indicators.note: uncovered means stripped of its covering, so each following word loses its outside letters

blocks.note: the inside two letters of this word
the inside two letters of this word
the inside two letters of this word

explanation.surface: Someone tracing where a stronger gale came from, as if exposing its source.
explanation.walkthrough: The one indicator applies to all three following words: each sheds its first and last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An origin is the point from which something arises, a synonym for its source.

clue.text: Wide-ranging Celtic playing to contain City

indicators.note: a team playing is moving around the pitch, so the team name's letters are moved around
to contain is to hold within, so the second piece is placed inside the first

blocks.note: the Glasgow football club, taken as written
EC is the postcode of the City of London, the financial district

explanation.surface: A football report: Celtic, playing an expansive game, keep Manchester City in check.
explanation.walkthrough: City here is not a football club but the City of London, the financial district, whose postcode is the usual crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclectic tastes draw from a broad variety of sources, so the word is a synonym for wide-ranging.

clue.text: Drinking stool, top to bottom, is striking

indicators.note: in a down answer, moving the top to the bottom shifts the leading letter of the word to its end

blocks.note: downing a drink is swallowing it quickly
taken as written, its first letter to be moved

explanation.surface: Someone knocking back drinks at the bar, a stool tipped over.
explanation.walkthrough: The S at the front of STOOL goes to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Downing tools is the idiom for stopping work, especially in a walkout, so it means being on strike.

clue.text: Heartless neocon seeing the light

indicators.note: without a heart, so the central letters of the word that follows are taken out

blocks.note: a neoconservative, taken as written

explanation.surface: A hard-hearted neoconservative politician finally sees the light and changes their views.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the middle two letters OC from the six-letter word; the phrase 'seeing the light' hides a definition of a glowing gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Neon is the gas in glowing advertising tubes, so it stands for the light those signs give off.

clue.text: Follow instructions to safeguard door's intricacy

indicators.note: to safeguard something is to keep it protected inside, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: to comply is to do as told
an exit is a door out

explanation.surface: A security notice: obey these rules to protect the complicated door mechanism.
explanation.definitionFit: Complexity is the state of being intricate, so the two nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: A vault redesigned indeed made cheaper

indicators.note: redesigned means drawn up afresh, so the letters before it take a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
read as two words, in deed: the word deed with the rearranged letters going in it

explanation.surface: A bank vault was remodelled to save money on the building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indeed' must be split into 'in deed' to reveal the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To devaluate, a variant of devalue, is to reduce in value, so in past tense made cheaper.

clue.text: Cause of inflation with little money for bread

blocks.note: something that pumps up a tyre or balloon is what makes it inflate
a nickel is a five-cent coin, a small sum

explanation.surface: An economics remark: rising prices mean a small coin buys less bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inflation' wants to mean rising prices, with money and bread fitting that picture; it is literal inflation, as of a tyre.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumpernickel is a dark, dense German rye loaf, an example of bread.

clue.text: Excellent high mark (on the bedpost)

blocks.note: top means uppermost, highest
a notch on the bedpost is a cut tallying a romantic conquest

explanation.surface: A boast about an outstanding new tally scored on the bedpost.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-notch is an informal adjective for first-rate, of the highest quality.

clue.text: How to hide broken heart saying goodbye here?

indicators.note: to hide something is to put it out of sight inside another thing, so one piece wraps the other
something broken has its parts knocked apart, so the next word's letters are scattered

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A tearful farewell: how can one hide a heartbreak while waving someone off?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: an airport is a place of farewells. HEATHROW is London's main airport.
explanation.definitionFit: Heathrow, London's busiest airport, is a place where travellers and friends say goodbye to each other.

clue.text: Attractive European somewhere in the arctic circle

blocks.note: a magnetic personality attracts people
a Pole is a person from Poland

explanation.surface: A charming continental visitor found somewhere north of the Arctic Circle.
explanation.definitionFit: The north magnetic pole, where compasses point, lies in the high Arctic, a location within that region.

clue.text: Run from a cholecystectomy?

definitions.note: cryptic: read as two words, the operation itself

blocks.note: first meaning: a horse's fastest pace, or to move at it
second meaning, split in two: a cholecystectomy is surgery on the gall bladder

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical reading: split the answer as GALL OP, a surgical procedure on the gall bladder.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallop is a fast run, especially a horse's fastest gait; the second part is a pun on surgery.

clue.text: Shed a tear in polluted air — it's a weather feature

indicators.note: in means placed within, so the first piece goes inside the second
polluted means contaminated and spoilt, so the letters of the next word are disturbed

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
to sob is to weep

explanation.surface: Someone weeping over smog-laden air in a city, a sad sign of the weather.
explanation.definitionFit: An isobar is a line on a weather map joining places of equal atmospheric pressure, a standard meteorological feature.

clue.text: Listen to weird USA sect getting regularly rattled

indicators.note: weird means strange or out of the ordinary, so the letters that follow are put in an unusual order
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the next word is kept

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a cult is a religious sect
the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Eavesdrop on a strange American cult that keeps getting shaken up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weird USA sect' looks like one anagram, but only USA is rearranged; the sect is a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Auscultate is the medical term for listening to the body's internal sounds, typically through a stethoscope.

clue.text: Ravel covered in banknotes

indicators.note: something covered in a wrapper sits inside it, so the answer lies within the next word

blocks.note: letters three to six of this word

explanation.surface: The composer Ravel smothered in paper money, as if paid handsomely.
explanation.walkthrough: Ravel looks like the French composer, but here it is a verb meaning to tangle.
explanation.definitionFit: To ravel is to entangle, and to knot is likewise to tie or tangle threads together.

clue.text: See 3
False alibi not a result of drink

indicators.note: something false is not genuine and has been fabricated, so the letters are made up into something else

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A defendant's phony alibi was not, after all, the consequence of being drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A libation is an alcoholic drink, jocularly, or one poured as an offering to a deity.

clue.text: Non-drinker gets into German beer, not lager

indicators.note: gets into means enters, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: Bier is the German word for beer
TT stands for teetotal, someone who abstains from alcohol

explanation.surface: A teetotaller starts drinking German ale, but avoids lager.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits at the end and leans on the word beer that also ends the wordplay; bitter is a British pale ale, not a lager.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitter is a hoppy British ale served from the cask, a style of beer distinct from lager.

clue.text: March to secure one's utopia

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast within, so one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: to parade is to march in procession
the Roman numeral for one
the S of the possessive, taken as written

explanation.surface: Protesters marching to win their idea of a perfect society.
explanation.definitionFit: A utopia is an imagined perfect place, which is what paradise is.

clue.text: Family member is born, and that's a relief

blocks.note: né is the French-derived word for born, used of a man's original name
the exclamation you make when relieved

explanation.surface: A baby joins the family safely, and everyone is relieved.
explanation.definitionFit: A nephew is a sibling's son, so he belongs to the wider family.
